questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the single point of failure in a Failover Cluster Instance (FCI) configuration?
options: The shared storage — every node reads and writes the same disks, so a storage failure takes the whole cluster down
The Windows Server Failover Clustering service itself
The network card on the primary node only
FCI has no single point of failure by design
questions.explain: FCI nodes share the same storage, so FCI is an instance-redundancy technology, not a data-redundancy one — losing the shared storage takes down every node at once.

questions.q: Why does replication not qualify as a real HA/DR failover technology, per this lesson?
options: Because replication exists to distribute data for reporting or offloading, not to provide a clean, failover-ready copy of the primary
Because replication is only available in the cloud
Because replication is functionally identical to log shipping
Because replication always requires manual data entry
questions.explain: Replication's design goal is distributing data across servers, not maintaining a synchronized failover target — a subscriber can drift from the publisher in ways that make it an imperfect failover copy.

questions.q: What is the main tradeoff of log shipping compared to Availability Groups, according to this lesson?
options: Log shipping failover is a manual, scripted process with a real data-loss window, versus AG's potential for automatic, near-instant failover
Log shipping cannot work across long distances
Log shipping requires more expensive licensing than AGs in every case
Log shipping and AGs have identical failover characteristics
questions.explain: Log shipping tolerates distance and latency well but requires manual failover and has a data-loss window based on how recently logs were shipped and restored.

questions.q: What underlying dependency do both Availability Groups (in the typical Windows configuration) and FCI share, per this lesson?
options: Windows Server Failover Clustering (WSFC)
SQL Server Replication Services
A cloud-only load balancer
The tempdb database on shared storage
questions.explain: Both AGs (on Windows) and FCI rely on WSFC as the underlying clustering service, though AGs use independent storage per replica while FCI nodes share storage.

questions.q: A team wants one technology to protect a single SQL Server instance from a node crashing tonight, without needing a second copy of the data on separate storage. Which technology fits, per this lesson?
options: FCI — it moves the instance to a surviving node using the same shared storage, without requiring a separate data copy
Replication — it's designed exactly for this scenario
Log shipping — it provides instant automatic failover
None of the four technologies can address a node crash
questions.explain: FCI is built for exactly this case: surviving a node failure using shared storage, without maintaining a second independent copy of the data as AGs, log shipping, or replication would.
